text: For the choir director. To the tune of "The Lily of the Covenant." A miktam of David, for teaching.
When he fought Aram Naharaim and Aram Zobah, and when Joab returned and struck down twelve thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
God, you have rejected us and broken through our ranks; you were angry with us—now restore us!
You shook the land and split it open; heal its fractures, for it is tottering.
You made your people endure hard things; you gave us wine that left us reeling.
Yet you have given those who fear you a banner to rally to, raised up for the sake of truth. Selah

versions.text: Yet you have given those who fear you a banner to rally to, a refuge from the bow. Selah
versions.explanation: The Hebrew text reads קֹשֶׁט ("truth"), not קֶשֶׁת ("bow"), and there is no word for "refuge" in the verse. The current rendering follows a conjectural emendation and adds content. If the "bow" reading is retained, it should at least be marked in a footnote rather than presented as the text.

text: So that those you love may be rescued, save with your right hand and answer me.

versions.text: Save us with your right hand and answer me, so that those you love may be delivered.
versions.explanation: The reordering places the purpose clause last, weakening the Hebrew flow, and the added object "us" in "save us" clashes awkwardly with the singular "answer me" in the same line. Keeping the clause order of the Hebrew avoids the mixed pronouns. (A footnote could note that some manuscripts read "answer us.")

text: God has spoken in his holiness: "I will exult! I will parcel out Shechem and measure off the Valley of Succoth.

versions.text: God has spoken from his holiness: "I will exult! I will parcel out Shechem and measure off the Valley of Succoth.
versions.explanation: The preposition בְּ means "in" (i.e., "in his holiness" or "in his sanctuary"). "From his holiness" is an unnatural English phrase and shifts the sense of the Hebrew.

text: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the helmet on my head, Judah my scepter.
Moab is my washbasin; on Edom I hurl my sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph."
Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
Have you not rejected us, God? Will you not march out with our armies, God?
Give us help against the enemy, for human deliverance is worthless.
With God we will do mighty deeds, and he will trample our enemies down.
